source.title: Navigating the Safety Landscape: Measuring Risks in Finetuning Large Language Models
source.authors: Sheng-Hsuan Peng; Pin-Yu Chen; Matthew Hull; Duen Horng Chau

record.tranche_reason: Directly repeats harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful-prompt ASR evaluation, using Qi et al.'s examples and recipe on aligned chat models; it also evaluates related jailbreak attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful fine-tuning ASRs and jailbreak-prompt ASRs. Its system-prompt and random-weight-perturbation results are mainly reported as VISAGE safety-landscape measurements, not as tests of the specific prefilled-opening, decoding, token-position, or parameter-localization claims. It does not measure per-token KL divergence. Cited results from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: Section 4.2 fine-tunes LLaMA2-7B-chat and Vicuna-7B-v1.5 on 10/50/100 of Qi et al.'s harmful examples with their recipe (full-parameter, five epochs). It reports AdvBench ASR before and after, which is a direct replication of V1. Its other experiments (safety basin, system prompts, jailbreaks under weight perturbation) measure related constructs, not the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The central conclusion is a universal 'safety basin': random weight perturbations preserve aligned safety locally, with a sharp drop outside. The VISAGE score derived from it predicts vulnerability to harmful fine-tuning (LLaMA2 more robust than Vicuna). Harmful fine-tuning drags the model out of the basin, while harmful+safe mixing keeps it inside. System prompts strongly affect basin safety, with the LLaMA2 prompt helping universally. Jailbreak prompts are highly sensitive to weight perturbation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Qi et al.'s harmful samples and fine-tuning recipe, with full-parameter fine-tuning for five epochs; evaluates LLaMA2-7B-chat and Vicuna-7B-v1.5 at 10, 50, and 100 examples and reports AdvBench results for both 80 and 520 prompts. It also tests a harmful-plus-safe data mixture.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning ASR varies with example count, model, and evaluation-set size. Jailbreak results vary with model-weight perturbations; the paper also reports a system-prompt effect for Vicuna.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on 100 harmful plus 100 safe examples keeps ASR near the aligned level (0–1.3%), versus 95–100% for harmful-only training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixing safety data into harmful fine-tuning prevents loss of refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Jailbreak (GCG/PAIR) prompts that work on aligned LLaMA2/Vicuna fail on some randomly weight-perturbed variants. The LLaMA2 system prompt lowers Vicuna's jailbreak ASR across its local region.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak success is fragile to small random weight perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: Random weight perturbations keep the aligned safety level inside a local 'safety basin', with a step-like drop outside it. The VISAGE basin score ranks models' vulnerability to harmful fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligned models sit in a flat safety basin in weight space whose depth predicts fine-tuning risk.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The main harmful fine-tuning results cover two models. The jailbreak text reports a small subset of six prompts for LLaMA2, and several perturbation-curve values are only shown in figures. Main ASR evaluation uses refusal-keyword detection.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded VISAGE scores for system-prompt and random-weight landscape experiments because they are safety-margin metrics rather than the specific behaviours measured by the claim versions. No relevant per-token KL, compliant-prefix, decoding-change, or localized-parameter results are reported.

untested.parts: Only two 7B open models are tested, with no closed or larger models. ASR uses refusal-keyword detection only for the fine-tuning results, and no harmfulness score is given.
No benign-only or ordinary-utility fine-tuning is run.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, decoding changes, or isolated suffix attack on unselected prompts.
No localization of safety to a few weights or ranks. Random full-weight perturbation is not localization.
No test of data or objective causes of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Only V1 is genuinely tested, and it is supported. The reader's V2 'challenges' label is wrong: the mix condition is a safety-data mitigation, not benign fine-tuning. The V4 labels are dropped because the jailbreak prompts are a preselected successful subset with pooled GCG/PAIR, and the perturbation results concern weight sensitivity rather than opening bypass. The Fig. 2a base→chat interpolation is a whole-response ASR, not per-token KL, so it does not bear on V3. Fine-tuning ASR relies on refusal-keyword detection, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests harmful fine-tuning with 10, 50, and 100 examples on two models; it does not test every training size or model covered by the claim.
It tests 100 harmful examples mixed with 100 safe examples, not benign-only fine-tuning or ordinary benign instruction data on its own.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
It evaluates JailbreakBench attacks generated by GCG and PAIR, but not a prefilled compliant opening or decoding changes; it does not isolate a suffix mechanism.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
It describes fine-tuning as moving a model away from a safety basin, but does not test whether the data or training objective produces first-token shallowness.
No training intervention intended to spread safety beyond the first tokens, or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuning on 100 harmful examples plus 100 safe examples for ten epochs.
rows.note: The table's mix column is described as harmful and safe data; it reports a lower ASR than 100-shot harmful-only fine-tuning.
rows.check: Mixing 100 safe examples into harmful fine-tuning is a mitigation condition, not benign fine-tuning. It cannot show whether benign data raises harmful compliance, so it does not bear on V2. The comparison to harmful-only training is a defence result. The mix was also trained ten epochs versus five.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Evaluation on JailbreakBench prompts generated by GCG and PAIR.
rows.note: The authors report 4 successful prompts out of the 6 in the stated attackable subset.
rows.check: The 6 prompts are the JailbreakBench subset already known to succeed on LLaMA2, so the 4/6 (66.67%) is a re-check of a selected set, not a rate of attack success. GCG suffixes and PAIR rewrites are pooled, so the value cannot isolate a suffix or opening-bypass effect. The baseline is not applicable.

labels.reason: R1–R12 match Table 1: baseline ASR is 0–5%, rises to 85.2–95.0% after 10 examples, and increases further with 50 and 100 examples.

relation.reason: The study directly measures safety degradation after fine-tuning on 10, 50, and 100 harmful examples.

tranche.reason: Sections 4.1–4.2 reuse Qi et al.'s harmful examples and training hyperparameters for full-parameter fine-tuning, then measure harmful-response ASR before and after training.

source_check.notes: Capability and fluency checks concern randomly perturbed models, not the harmful-finetuned checkpoints in Table 1. Appendix B validates the safety-basin finding with LLaMAGuard 2; Table 1 uses keyword ASR.

statements.correction: Overlapping-author test; NeurIPS 2024; publicly available code. Five-epoch full-parameter fine-tuning on 10 harmful examples; AdvBench 520 keyword ASR: LLaMA2-7B-chat 0.2%→85.2%; Vicuna-7B-v1.5 2.5%→89.2%. Table 1 reports no uncertainty estimates.
statements.problem: The test is incorrectly called independent: Pin-Yu Chen coauthors this study and the original Qi et al. paper, reference [37].

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: ASR rises to high values after harmful-example fine-tuning across both models and evaluation sets (R1-R12).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: 100 harmful examples mixed with 100 safe examples, compared with 100 harmful examples alone
reader_labels.reason: The mixed-data condition has much lower ASR than harmful-only fine-tuning on both models and both evaluation sets; this does not establish the effect of benign-only fine-tuning (R13-R16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: JailbreakBench GCG/PAIR prompts on aligned LLaMA2-7B-chat
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports 4 successful prompts among the stated subset of 6, giving 66.67% ASR (R17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: JailbreakBench attacks under random weight perturbations, with the reported Vicuna system-prompt comparison
reader_labels.reason: Attack success is sensitive to weight perturbations, with some perturbed LLaMA2 models safer; the LLaMA2 prompt improves Vicuna's local-region safety (R18-R20).
